title: Original-ball paths in Teichmüller space: an elementary corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi
actual: Read all three exact PDF pages as text and rendered pixels, and full controlling TeX, checked exact copies in the versioned package.
proof: For a fixed closed oriented surface of genus g≥2, every pair in any closed ball of the marked Teichmüller metric admits a continuous rectifiable path inside that very ball of length ≤d_T(x,y)+4c_g. This gives the distance-two criterion in Farb's Question 3.5.

For R<c, join through the center. For R≥c, retreat each endpoint along a minimizing radial segment by min(c,r), choose a geodesic between the retreated points, and then reverse the second retreat. The published radial excursion c fits the middle segment inside R. The triangle inequality counts each retreat at most twice. Includes R=c, R=0, c=0, coincident points and center endpoints.

Kerckhoff's half-log supremum of extremal-length ratios transfers the fixed-topology Lenzhen–Rafi estimate, since the maximum of two endpoint ratios is uniformly bounded after division by the positive center extremal length. The journal theorem fixes the appropriate intermediate variable; the historical arXiv version has different numbering and an apparent endpoint label typo.

The result concerns the original metric and arbitrary rectifiable paths. A minimizing segment may leave the ball (Fortier Bourque–Rafi). The dual wall result of Petyt–Zalloum is in a different metric and there is no comparison of constants. No genus-uniform or optimal constant, mapping class group solution, or firstness asserted.
